answer: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, if you hit a person while reversing your car in a manner deemed rash or negligent, you could be charged under Section 281. This section states that such actions endangering human life can lead to imprisonment for up to six months, a fine of up to one thousand rupees, or both (Section 281 Body, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023). If the incident results in the death of the person, you could be charged under Section 106, which prescribes imprisonment for up to five years and a fine for causing death through rash or negligent acts not amounting to culpable homicide (Section 106(1), Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023).
summary_answer: If you accidentally hit a person with your car while reversing, you may face punishment under Section 281 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for rash or negligent driving, which could result in imprisonment for up to six months, a fine, or both. If the incident causes death, the penalties could be more severe under Section 106.

This section states that such actions endangering human life can lead to imprisonment for up to six months, a fine of up to one thousand rupees, or both (Section 281 Body, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023). If the incident results in the death of the person, you could be charged under Section 106, which prescribes imprisonment for up to five years and a fine for causing death through rash or negligent acts not amounting to culpable homicide (Section 106(1), Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023).
